name: Pacific Ocean
alt: A world map with a huge highlighted body of water spanning nearly half the globe.
facts: This is the biggest ocean — it's bigger than all the continents put together!
It's so wide that it touches Asia, Australia, and the Americas all at once.
It's home to the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point in any ocean.

name: Atlantic Ocean
alt: A world map with a highlighted body of water shaped like a long 'S', sitting between two groups of landmasses.
facts: This ocean separates the Americas from Europe and Africa.
It's the second largest ocean in the world, after the Pacific.
Ships and planes have crossed it for centuries, making it one of the most traveled oceans.

name: Indian Ocean
alt: A world map with a highlighted body of water bordered by land on three sides, north of the icy southern waters.
facts: This is the warmest ocean in the world.
It's the third largest ocean, named after the country of India along its coast.
Unlike most oceans, it's bordered by land on three sides instead of two.

name: Arctic Ocean
alt: A world map with a small highlighted body of water at the very top of the globe, mostly covered in ice.
facts: This is the smallest and coldest ocean, and parts of it are covered in ice.
It sits at the very top of the globe, around the North Pole.
Much of it freezes over in winter, and animals like polar bears hunt right on the ice.

name: Southern Ocean
alt: A world map with a highlighted ring of water encircling the icy landmass at the very bottom of the globe.
facts: This ocean surrounds Antarctica and is home to many penguins and whales.
It's the newest ocean to be officially recognized by name.
Strong winds and currents circle all the way around Antarctica here, uninterrupted by any other land.
